metadata.content: Georgia Hunter Bell: British 800m and 1500m runner celebrates team's female track success | Athletics News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Georgia Hunter Bell: British 800m and 1500m runner celebrates team's female track success Georgia Hunter Bell, Keely Hodgkinson, Amy Hunt and Dina Asher-Smith are standout members of a strong British female core delivering medals on the track; Hunter Bell: "We're locked into everyone's goals... someone winning or bringing home a medal, it makes you even more keen to do well" Thursday 8 October 2026 17:10, UK Image: Georgia Hunter Bell (left) and Keely Hodgkinson (right) celebrate after both winning gold at the World Athletics Indoor Championships in March Georgia Hunter Bell has enjoyed quite the year, winning a hat-trick of gold medals at the World Indoor Championships, for England at the Commonwealth Games, and again for Team GB at the European Championships. But British female track success in 2025 certainly didn't stop there. Sprinter Amy Hunt made headlines with a record four-gold display in the Europeans in Birmingham, while Dina Asher-Smith now tops the all-time medal table at the championships after winning her 11th, eight of which are gold. metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton has revealed Ferrari held a "huge discussion" to reflect on a strategic error at the Bahrain Grand Prix that he says "wasn't good enough".
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver says team held 'huge discussions' over strategy following Bahrain GP tyre-choice blunder | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver says team held 'huge discussions' over strategy following Bahrain GP tyre-choice blunder Lewis Hamilton plummeted from second on the grid after starting last weekend's Bahrain GP on slick dry tyres in wet conditions; watch Practice at 9.30am followed by Sprint Qualifying at 1.30pm on Friday live on Sky Sports F1 as the Singapore Grand Prix weekend begins Thursday 8 October 2026 15:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following criticisms at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Lewis Hamilton defends Ferrari strategists Lewis Hamilton has revealed Ferrari held a "huge discussion" to reflect on a strategic error at the Bahrain Grand Prix that he says "wasn't good enough". Ferrari fitted both Hamilton and his team-mate Charles Leclerc with slick dry tyres at last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix, which was being hosted in Malaysia and started on a wet track that the Italian squad anticipated would quickly dry out once the race began. The decision was proven wrong as Hamilton fell from his starting position of second to almost the back of the field in the opening stages, with the 14 of 22 drivers that started on the intermediate tyre gaining a huge advantage. messages.text: Scotland's Syme and Forrest among Open de Espana leaders

metadata.summary: Scotland's Connor Syme and Grant Forrest both made a five-under-par 66 to share a three-way lead after the opening round of the Open de Espana in Madrid, where Sergio Garcia sits just one shot back.
metadata.content: DP World Tour: Scotland's Connor Syme and Grant Forrest amongst leaders after first round of Open de España with Sergio Garcia one back | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content DP World Tour: Scotland's Connor Syme and Grant Forrest amongst leaders after first round of Open de España with Sergio Garcia one back There is a three-way tie for the lead after the first round of the Open de Espana; Sergio Garcia sits one shot back; The Open de Espana continues on Friday October 9 from 1pm on Sky Sports Golf Thursday 8 October 2026 21:56, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day one of the Open de Espana held at Club de Campo Villa de Madrid in Madrid, Spain Scotland's Connor Syme and Grant Forrest both made a five-under-par 66 to share a three-way lead after the opening round of the Open de Espana in Madrid, where Sergio Garcia sits just one shot back. Starting on the 10th, Syme made a quick start with back-to-back birdies then rolled in a 52-foot putt at the 15th as he headed into the turn five under. A tap-in birdie at the fourth saw Syme take the solo lead at Real Club de Campo Villa de Madrid, but he was then not able to save par on the eighth after finding the rough off the tee.
